english.title: Fail to keep records as req by reg 32(1), (2) or (3) in permanent and legible form and retain them for 3 year period
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) being a person required to keep a record by regulation

(A)_[32(2)]_
(B)_[32(3)]_

of the Animals and Animal Products (Examination for Residues and Maximum Residue Limits) Regulations 1997, namely **(..SPECIFY RECORD..) failed to

(C)_[keep that record in a permanent and legible form]_
(D)_[retain that record for a period of three years from the end of the calendar year to which such record relates]_
(E)_[retain a prescription intended to show that withdrawal periods had been observed, for a period of five years from the date of the commencement of the withdrawal period to which it related]_
english.legislation: Contrary to regulations 32(4) and 23 of the Animals and Animal Products (Examination for Residues and Maximum Residue Limits) Regulations 1997.

other.penalty:
Summary: A fine not exceeding the statutory maximum.
Indictment: A fine.

Time Limit on Prosecutions
No prosecution shall be begun after the expiry of -

(a) three years from commission of the offence; or
(b) one year from its discovery by the prosecutor,

whichever is the earlier.

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
